questions.q: Where should the highest-level information go on a dashboard for most audiences?
options: Always in the exact center of the page
The bottom-right corner
It doesn't matter where information is placed
The top-left corner, since most audiences read top to bottom, left to right
questions.explain: Placement should follow natural reading order — the headline fact goes where the eye lands first, with detail increasing as it moves further.

questions.q: How does a card visual help establish visual hierarchy?
options: It hides all other visuals on the page
Its large size signals importance before a viewer has even processed what the number means
It automatically applies conditional formatting to every other visual
Cards can only be used for the least important metric on a page
questions.explain: A number rendered large reads as more important than the same number in small type — size alone does the communicating, no extra decoration needed.

questions.q: Why should a dashboard avoid scrollbars?
options: Power BI technically cannot render scrollbars on dashboards
Scrollbars are fine as long as there are fewer than ten tiles
Scrollbars only appear on mobile devices
Dashboards are meant to be absorbed at a glance, so everything needs to fit on one screen without scrolling
questions.explain: If a dashboard needs scrolling, that's a sign some content belongs in a full report instead, or one click deeper via drillthrough — not crammed onto the dashboard.

questions.q: In the Sales and Marketing sample dashboard, what pattern does the layout follow?
options: The most detailed chart is placed in the top-left corner
All tiles are arranged in random order with no intentional pattern
Tiles are ordered alphabetically by their title
The top-left tile shows the single highest-level number, with tiles growing progressively more specific moving right and down
questions.explain: Total Volume — the headline number — sits top-left, with the trend line, segment breakdown, and more specific detail following the natural reading path.

questions.q: Why should chart scales, axis ordering, and colors stay consistent across a dashboard?
options: It only matters if the dashboard has more than five tiles
Power BI requires all visuals to use identical colors by default
Consistency is only a cosmetic preference with no functional benefit
So a viewer doesn't have to relearn a visual convention on every tile — inconsistency forces re-interpretation from scratch each time
questions.explain: Once a viewer learns what a color or scale means on one tile, keeping it consistent lets that understanding carry over instead of resetting for every visual.
